observed_text:
Within Timken's roller-bearing discussion, the source states that false brinelling will actually wear away the surface texture, whereas the original surface texture will remain in the depression of a true brinell; the page 18 example caption describes the pictured indentations as true metal deformation and not wear as with false brinelling, with grinding marks still visible in the groove [EV-K01-004]. This is a qualitative physical-surface inspection cue that requires examining the actual depression or wear area, and the page 19 discussion concerns stationary slight axial rolling-element movement and very small reversing angular oscillation in roller bearings [EV-K01-004]. The supplied CWT/category input cannot establish which texture is physically present here: the module input is a caller-assigned class/task with no actual classifier or task-model inference, and the scenario cause (external vibration during standstill) is an independently specified teaching assumption, not an observation [EV-K01-001]. The NSK example likewise attributes raceway false brinelling on a deep-groove ball bearing outer ring to external vibration while stationary, but it is a manufacturer example, not an observation of a CWRU sample [EV-K01-001]. Inspection guidance calls for examining raceways and external surfaces after thorough cleaning, but it gives directions rather than a complete reuse or rejection rule [EV-K01-010].

Evidence limitations:
The texture comparison is a qualitative inspection cue with no quantitative threshold and is not a CWT image criterion; identification cannot be completed from an outer-ring class alone [EV-K01-004].
The NSK false-brinelling attribution is a manufacturer case example for a deep-groove ball bearing outer ring under external vibration while stationary; it does not show that all outer-ring faults share this mechanism or that any project sample had this condition [EV-K01-001].
The scenario cause is an independently specified teaching assumption, not a source-proven sample fact or classifier inference [EV-K01-001].
The inspection card is not a complete reuse or rejection list and cannot alone support reuse, replacement or release decisions; no model-specific limits or aviation applicability conclusions are provided [EV-K01-010].
Evidence scope is registered generic bearing education only, with no model-specific or aviation/reuse authorization; actual device records, lubricant identity/specification/batch, sampling quantity and model-specific thresholds were not supplied.
